rationale: bugs_open/450 (090 diagnosis CONFIRMED, run 96e97dc4, 2026-09-02 22:11Z). A site plan names tool pages (pages.page_type='tool') with generic sections BEFORE any component_level='tool' component exists — tools arrive from the ~3h design rotation hours-to-days later, under names the planner never saw (seotools.co.uk: 0 of 7 planned names matched what tool-deployer eventually built). The plan-side hold (owned_page_review, filed by ReconcileSitePlanAction) has no consumer. Five generic producers then route the page to page-build-handler, whose guard asked only whether pages.rebuild_policy='owned'; a planned tool page is 'generic', so the guard passed it and the generic builder wrote exactly what the plan said — prose about the tool — and deployed it. All seven seotools URLs then served 200 at ~56 KB with the tool's own headline and ZERO <form>/<input>. Control the same morning: advertise.co.uk, whose rotation happened to reach it BEFORE its plan persisted, so the plan named real tool components and nothing went wrong — ordering luck was the only difference. Fleet census, re-run 2026-09-03 and identical to the filing figure: 61 tool-type deployed pages with no tool-level component across 10 sites. Every status-shaped check passes on such a page (page active/deployed, components deployed, URL 200, link checkers self-clearing); only the served body tells the truth, because a tool is a FORM and never a size. THE INTENT: make 'a tool page with no tool on it' refuse generic builds, at the seams every producer crosses, with the verdict DERIVED from the page's contents rather than stored as a flag. Derivation is the whole design and it rests on a measurement, not a preference: pages.rebuild_policy is CHECK-constrained to 'generic'|'owned' (migration 164) and NOTHING in this estate has ever UPDATEd it — two INSERT-time writers, no transition in any handler, check or scheduler, in either direction. A flag set at plan time is therefore a flag nobody clears, and the page would be protected for ever. A derived predicate lifts by itself the instant tool-deployer inserts the component. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, stated so the scope is not over-read: it does not repair or remove the 61 existing shells (realised pages; cleanup is instance work owned by the portfolio_positioning lane), it does not stop the PLANNER naming tool pages (that is the sibling plan-side arm enforce_tool_sources, bugs_open/444's gate generalised, still to land and deliberately a separate commit with its own key), and it does not gate rerender_single_page's re-assembly of existing components (migration 164 calls that the sanctioned owned-page deploy path; gating it is the bugs_open/210 family). PROCESS NOTE, declared rather than hidden: this submission FOLLOWS the commit (587666be8) instead of preceding it. Another lane's pathspec commit took a half-finished hunk of this rename as a same-file passenger while the rest was still dirty, so HEAD called three uncommitted symbols and make build-* was broken fleet-wide; repairing that could not wait ~30 minutes for a verdict. The commit carries no Council-Reviewed trailer and makes no review claim.

plan.summary: A tool page with no tool component must not be built by the generic builder. pageIsOwnedForGuard becomes pageRefusesGenericBuild, returning a two-class verdict (owned | tool_pending) instead of a bool: the question was never 'is this page owned' but 'may the generic builder write it', and that has two independent NO answers. The tool_pending class is derived in SQL (page_type='tool' AND NOT EXISTS a live component_level='tool' row), rides the door's existing primary-key read as a second output column, and is consulted at the writeWorkItem policy door (parks at file time, before LLM spend), load_page_record's refuse_owned_page arm (which drains the ~339 unbuilt_internal_link rows ALREADY queued against shells, that a write-time door cannot see), save_page_sections, AssemblePageAction, the rerender escalation and the build-selection exclusion. Receipts carry the refusal_class and stop asserting rebuild_policy='owned' on a page that is 'generic'. Kill switch DISABLE_TOOL_SHELL_REFUSAL ships ARMED and scopes to the new arm only.

edits.rationale: The file's own doctrine is that it is the ONLY place a pipeline may read build policy, so the widened question belongs here rather than in a sibling predicate — two predicates for 'may we build this' is exactly the drift the reuse_agent seat objected to when this file first duplicated the save path's inline query. pageIsOwnedForGuard is RENAMED rather than kept alongside a new function, deliberately: the rename compile-forces all four call sites to be re-read, so none can keep asking the narrower question by accident. The SQL fragment has ONE rendering because it now decides whether five producers may write a page. It deliberately does NOT reuse discovery_checks.toolEligibilityWhere, which looks similar but also requires the page to carry exactly ONE component (it answers 'is this a ported tool whose identity we must infer'); the 450 shells carry two components and would be invisible to it.

This is the seam EVERY work-item write crosses (insertWorkItem wraps it; discovery sweeps, config-driven steps and direct Go callers all pass through), which is why the owned-page and growth-posture doors already live here. Parking at file time costs no LLM spend at all. The ordering argument is unchanged and preserved: the boring PK read still gates the novel jsonpath SQL, which now runs for pages refused for EITHER reason rather than only owned ones. The declaration probe is untouched — refuse_owned_page keeps meaning 'this handler will not build a page it is not allowed to build', and page-build-handler remains its sole declarer, so livespec's pin needs no edit. builder_needed gets a DIFFERENT value for the new class on purpose: it is the roadmap sweep's GROUPING key, and telling that sweep these findings await an owned-page content route would send a human to build the wrong thing — they await a TOOL.

The selection-level exclusion is where the owned fix put most of the load for the two loops with the highest traffic, and a tool shell must not be handed to a generic build loop for the same reason an owned page must not. ownedPageExclusionSQL is kept BYTE-IDENTICAL and the new clause appended around it rather than folded in, so anything pinning that literal keeps matching and the owned arm can still be read on its own. include_owned=true still drops both, unchanged.

This is the seam that matters most for the EXISTING backlog, and it is the reason the write-time door alone is insufficient: ~339 unbuilt_internal_link rows are already queued against shell pages and a door that runs at file time cannot see them. They arrive here, and refusing at load spends no LLM tokens on a page whose save would be refused anyway (this arm exists because bugs_closed/301 measured exactly that waste for the owned class). The opt-in stays opt-in and its sole declarer is unchanged.

The backstop: page-build-handler has no assemble step, so an item can reach the save directly. The refusal stays an ERROR here (the save genuinely did not happen, and reporting otherwise would be worse) and still leads with ownedPageSkipReasonPrefix, which is what UpdateWorkItemStatusAction reads to choose wont_fix over failed. The OWNED wording is preserved byte-for-byte because a live operator query and a pinned test both read it; the new class gets its own text, because telling someone their page is rebuild_policy=owned when the column says 'generic' sends them to check a column that disagrees with the row.

assemble_page is the one seam meaning 'generic composition about to be committed to the site repo', used by exactly the three loops that compose-then-commit. The refusal must stay the SKIP shape (git_commit's checkUpstreamSkipped already honours it) and not become an error: no build loop sets continue_on_error, so an error here strands every remaining page. The OWNED_PAGE_GUARD_UNCHECKED fail-open window keeps its existing error code and count — the window is the same window, only the question widened — so no finding-code registry entry is needed.

Same argument one step along: an owned page's empty content_data is its normal state, and so is a tool page's while it waits for its tool — escalating to the writer is precisely what would fill those slots with prose about the missing tool. A distinct disposition (skipped_tool_pending_page) rather than reusing skipped_owned_page, so the two suppressed populations stay countable apart; the bugs_open/454 lane was told, because its work reads these dispositions.

EVERY fixture scripts a 'generic' page — the exact row the old guard waved through — so a test that passed against the old code would prove nothing about this change; a fixture scripting 'owned' would be vacuous. The pair carrying the design is ParkedAtDeferred plus ToolPageWithItsToolIsUntouched: same page type, same handler, same finding, differing ONLY in whether a tool component exists, which is the self-clearing property stated as a test rather than as a comment. The parked error text is RENDERED from ownedPageParkedItem itself rather than transcribed (the neighbouring door test's coupling idiom). The file header carries the mutation protocol and the guards-in-series warning, because four guards here stop the same work and killing one proves nothing if a later one catches it.

grounded_in: bugs_open/450 §Symptom: 'At 21:1xZ all seven /tools/<slug>/index.html serve 200 at ~56 KB with the tool's own headline and 0 <form>, 0 <input>, 0 <select>, 1 <button> (the mobile-menu toggle). Control, identical probe: advertise.co.uk's three real tools carry 1 form, 0-11 inputs, up to 2 selects, 4 scripts.'

090 verdict (run 96e97dc4, CONFIRMED 2026-09-02 22:11:33Z): 'The owned-page guard that should refuse a generic save (pageIsOwnedForGuard, owned_page_guard.go:176-190, called from save_page_sections_action.go:186) reads pages.rebuild_policy='owned', which a planned tool page never carries (it is 'generic' — and so are tool pages built by tool-deployer), so 'owned' in the plan validator and 'owned' in the save guard are two different predicates and the hold protects nothing.'

owned_page_guard.go, the doctrine this change preserves: 'This is the ONLY place any pipeline may read ownership policy from ... two predicates for "is this page owned" is precisely the drift class this guard exists to prevent, and the council's reuse_agent seat objected on exactly that ground when this file first duplicated the save path's inline query.'

migration 164_pages_rebuild_policy.sql:24-25: "ALTER TABLE pages ADD COLUMN rebuild_policy text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'generic' CONSTRAINT pages_rebuild_policy_check CHECK (rebuild_policy IN ('generic', 'owned'))" — with no later migration altering that CHECK, and zero UPDATE ... rebuild_policy statements anywhere in Go (verified by grep across platform/): the measurement that rules out a stored flag.

deploy_tool_action.go: the tool page_components INSERT at :517 precedes raiseToolContentItem at :564 — the ordering that makes the derived predicate already false when the tool pipeline raises its own companion item, so this change cannot deadlock the add_tool wave the portfolio_positioning lane is running against these same pages.

The link repair is the one that fires FIRST on a fresh remake; it is not the only door.' — the evidence for guarding the shared seams rather than the one detector.

bugs_open/220:222-228, on why the detector cannot route by page_type itself: 'availableBuilders lives in package actions, which imports discovery_checks, so the check cannot reach it without a leaf-package refactor' — verified still true 2026-09-03.

Fleet census re-run 2026-09-03 (identical to the 2026-09-02 filing figure): 61 deployed page_type='tool' pages with no component_level='tool' component, across loanandmortgagecalculator.co.uk 16, webdesign.co.uk 14, loanzy.uk 11, seotools.co.uk 7, loancash.co.uk 3, idea.uk 3, vonc.com 3, leopardessconsulting.co.uk 2, cv1.co.uk 1, boxingonline.com 1. Queue state same day: 339 unresolved unbuilt_internal_link rows, 171 open owned_page_review holds.
plan.risks: 1) FALSE REFUSAL FROM A MISLABELLED page_type. The predicate inherits page_type's classifier gaps: a page wrongly typed 'tool' with no tool component is refused. The failure is LOUD (one deduped owned_page_review naming the retype remedy; parked items keep their item_key and dispatch again once corrected) and never a silent shell, which is the direction of error this change is for. Reviewer check worth making: is there a live population of mislabelled tool-typed pages whose generic rebuild is actually wanted? I did not census this and mark it [UNMEASURED]. Note I initially cited 578_retype_mislabelled_tool_rows_HOLD.sql as evidence such pages exist — that migration retypes page_components, NOT pages.page_type, and nothing in the tree retypes page rows; the citation was wrong and is withdrawn here rather than repeated. 2) PORTED TOOLS LIVING INLINE in a non-tool-level component are classed as shells and refused. This is protective (a generic rebuild would clobber the inline tool) and most such pages are already rebuild_policy='owned' via adopt_verbatim, but it is a behaviour change on adopted sites and is stated rather than discovered. 3) THE EXISTING 61 SHELLS now refuse further generic rebuilds. Intended — they are already wrong and rebuilding them generically only rewrites the prose — but it means their queued items terminate wont_fix with receipts rather than 'succeeding', which will look like new failures in any dashboard counting terminal statuses. The portfolio_positioning lane owns their repair and has been told. 4) A SECOND OUTPUT COLUMN ON A HOT SEAM: the door's read is crossed by every work-item write. It stays ONE round trip (the EXISTS is a second select-list column on the same PK lookup) and the subplan executes only for tool-typed rows, but a reviewer should satisfy themselves the guardian seat's 333-era objection — 'the boring read gates the novel SQL' — still holds, since the boring read is now marginally less boring. 5) FAIL-OPEN IS UNCHANGED and so is its window: an unreadable row still means 'not refused', logged at ERROR and counted as OWNED_PAGE_GUARD_UNCHECKED at the assemble call site. A shell whose row cannot be read is still buildable. 6) SCOPE: 'tool' only. No component_level='game' exists anywhere, so a game arm could never self-clear; entity-page already routes to capability_gap via builderForPageType. Later arms are one disjunct each in a function. 7) NOT ADDRESSED, deliberately, and each is a separate piece of work: the plan-side supply of these stubs (enforce_tool_sources, the sibling of bugs_open/444's gate), the N-links-one-target rebuild churn (bugs_open/220's own candidate), the owned_page_review hold's continuing lack of a consumer, and rerender_single_page's re-assembly path (bugs_open/210 family).
